opportunities.title: Small Research Grants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: BES members; researchers from all countries globally; projects can be conducted anywhere in the world. Funding not available for salary of principal researcher, bench fees or direct costs of hiring departmental vehicles. Not a scholarship; cannot fund projects forming part of a funded fellowship or completion of an undergraduate/master's degree.
opportunities.summary: Provides up to £5,000 for new and innovative ecological research of the highest international standard, with a clear ecological science focus.

opportunities.title: Synthesis Grants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Main applicant must have BES membership; not required for all working group members. Groups of 8-15 individuals with diverse mix of career stages, institutions and international participation, demonstrating EDI principles.
opportunities.summary: Fast-tracking innovative and impactful research by funding up to £30k towards the formation of new two-year synthesis groups that bring together diverse interdisciplinary groups to focus on data analysis and synthesis.

opportunities.title: Long-term Research Grants

amount.raw: up to £500 per year for a decade of data collection (£3,500 for first five years, additional £3,500 in year six)

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must have BES membership. Open to all types of ecologists including conservation practitioners (e.g. Reserve Managers, consultants) and university academics. Awarded to individuals, not organisations.
opportunities.summary: Provides a small amount of funding each year for 10 years to enable existing short-term projects with 1-2 years of data to be funded into the long term, supporting long-term ecological studies anywhere in the world.

opportunities.title: Pedagogical Research and Development Grants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must have BES membership. Open to anyone involved in teaching ecology at any level (early years to lifelong learning, formal or informal settings), and those in industry exploring new teaching ideas. Awarded to individuals, not organisations. Projects max 12 months.
opportunities.summary: Funds research informing teaching and learning practices in ecology, providing up to £5k towards evidence-based learning to improve learners' experience and promote excellence in teaching.

opportunities.title: Connecting Ecologists with Other Disciplines Grants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must have BES membership. Open to PhD students, postdoctoral fellows, early career ecologists, established researchers or employees of other organisations. Undergraduates and masters students not eligible. Awarded to individuals, not organisations. Placements up to 12 months.
opportunities.summary: Promotes interdisciplinary skills by funding up to £20k towards placements (secondments) in different disciplines and sectors, immersing an ecologist in another professional world where ecology can make a difference.

opportunities.title: Outreach and Engagement Grants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Lead applicant must have BES membership. Open to individuals, teams and organisations across all experience levels. Projects max 12 months. No restrictions on where applicants come from or carry out work.
opportunities.summary: Provides funding of up to £2,000 for individuals, teams and organisations to engage public audiences with the excitement, importance and relevance of ecological science through outreach, public engagement and science communication activities.

opportunities.title: Training and Travel Grants

amount.raw: A maximum of £500 for events in person; a maximum of £250 for virtual conferences/courses

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must be a BES member and a PhD student or postgraduate researcher (PGR) registered on a postgraduate research degree programme. Postdoc researchers, undergraduates and masters students not eligible. Must work/study at a university or research institution.
opportunities.summary: Helps PhD students and postgraduate researchers meet the costs of specialist field training courses and the travel costs associated with presenting their work at workshops and conferences. Awarded on a lottery-based system.

opportunities.title: Annual Meeting Grants 2026
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must be a BES member at any career stage; must be a citizen of and based in the Global South; must be travelling from and returning to the Global South country; must have applied to present at the Annual Meeting; must be at least three years since last awarded a BES Training and Travel Grant.
opportunities.summary: Supports researchers based in Global South countries to attend the BES Annual Meeting in the UK, covering travel and costs directly related to attending the meeting (registration, transport, food, accommodation).
